name: Philip
overview: Philip was a male disciple of the Messiah and one of the Twelve apostles chosen by Jesus Christ. He hailed from the city of Bethsaida in Galilee, as noted in the Gospel of John. His role as a disciple and apostle highlights his close association with Christ during His earthly ministry.
namesAndTitles: Philip is the only recorded name for this individual and it is a proper name mentioned in Matthew 10:3. There is no special meaning or divine origin attributed to this name within the provided references.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Philip as both a disciple and an apostle of YHVH, the Messiah. Beyond these spiritual relationships, no family connections are recorded in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Philip's significance lies in his being one of the Twelve apostles personally chosen by Jesus, marking him as a foundational figure in the early Christian community. His origin from Bethsaida in Galilee connects him geographically to the region where Jesus conducted much of His ministry. As a disciple and apostle, Philip participated directly in the mission and teachings of Christ, contributing to the spread of the Gospel.
